gold-fill.purpose: The accent as a fill or a mark: the primary button, the focused pane's ring, checkboxes, sliders, selected text, the start screen's cursor. Ink on it is gold-fill-ink (#141414 on light).

field-line.purpose: A text field's border. The hairline on dark; on light a quiet grey at 3.0:1 on panel, since a white field on a near-white panel has nothing else to show where it is.

prompt.purpose: The start screen's ~/xtermium $ in JetBrains Mono (--t, weak), the $ in amber, a blinking amber block cursor after it; decorative, hidden from assistive tech.

headline.purpose: The lead sentence under the logo on the start screen: the system face, 600 at --t-xl, -0.025em.

title.purpose: Dialog and page titles (h2, --t-l) in the system face, 600, -0.01em; h3 is 600 at body size.

body.purpose: Default interface text in the system face, inherited from body: buttons, fields, field labels, rows, menus, tab names (--t).

body-strong.purpose: The focused tab's name in the title bar's field and the steps of Getting started, at 500. The active tab itself is not set heavier.

prose.purpose: Paragraphs and text areas; a line is as tall as a list row (line-height φ).

label.purpose: Counts, hints, secondary lines, the status bar and tags in the system face (--t-s).

mono.purpose: What is read character by character: code, kbd, pre, snippet commands, a host key's fingerprint, the sign-in code, the Co-op passcode, tunnel addresses and ring traffic figures in JetBrains Mono; always left to right.

shadows.name: --shadow-float
shadows.purpose: Bars floating over a view (find, reconnect) and the hint over a detached window.

shadows.name: --shadow-menu
shadows.purpose: Context menus, dropdown lists and toasts.

shadows.name: --shadow-dialog
shadows.purpose: Modal dialogs and the command palette.

motion.name: --ease-out
motion.purpose: Arrivals: fast to where they land, then settle.

motion.name: float-in
motion.purpose: Dialogs, the palette, find and reconnect bars, toasts, the start screen's logo: a fade from 5px short of where they hang (--from, -5px for top-hung).

motion.name: fade-in
motion.purpose: The scrim behind a dialog or the palette, and the lock screen.

motion.name: focus-ring
motion.purpose: The focused pane's ring glides to the next pane; no transition while an edge is dragged.

motion.name: toast-out
motion.purpose: A toast leaves faster than it came (Svelte out:fade, 0 under reduced motion).

motion.name: search-open
motion.purpose: The sidebar search field opens out from its button.

motion.name: caret
motion.purpose: A folder's caret turning open or closed.

motion.name: step-back
motion.purpose: Chrome dims to 45% while the sidebar search is open.

motion.name: drop-zone
motion.purpose: Pane drop zones lighting up under a dragged tab.

motion.name: blink
motion.purpose: The start screen's amber block cursor after the prompt.

motion.name: found
motion.purpose: A amber wash held, then fading off the setting a search went to (Settings.svelte).

motion.name: outline-breathe
motion.purpose: Broadcast outline style: a 16px inner glow swells and settles.

motion.name: outline-ring
motion.purpose: Broadcast outline style (also rainbow): a conic sweep around the pane.

motion.name: outline-march
motion.purpose: Broadcast outline style: 45° stripes walking along the edge.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every animation and transition collapses under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: outline-fade
motion.purpose: Broadcast outline style: the colour dims to 25% and back.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Operator's Rack"**

xtermium is a rack of live connections, in the brand's world: the operator's terminal of the website (xtermium.com) and the brand kit, carried into the app. The chrome is the website's near-black ground and surfaces, neutral and a hair apart, getting lighter the nearer they sit to the hand. Each kind of connection has its own hue, the way cables on a patch panel are colour-coded: SSH is cobalt, RDP violet, serial chartreuse. One phosphor amber accent marks where you are and what you picked. Nothing else is coloured, so a glance at the rack tells you which kind of session each row and tab is, and a glance at the amber tells you where the keyboard is. The start screen waits at the website's prompt, `~/xtermium $` and a blinking amber block cursor, over the brand kit's logo.

The feel is quiet and exact, as dense as a modern code editor: 13px text, 26px controls, 21px rows, small precise corners. The whole interface is in the system face, so the app reads as a native tool; JetBrains Mono, the brand's face, is kept for what is read character by character (code, commands, keys, fingerprints, passcodes). The sidebar (the session rack), the tab area with its panes, and the file panel are rounded panels floating a few pixels apart on a darker window. They are flat at rest and are told apart by tone and hairline, not by shadow. Only things that float above the work cast a shadow: menus, dialogs, the command palette, toasts.

Every proportion comes from the golden ratio (φ ≈ 1.618). Spacing steps along the Fibonacci scale, padding pairs keep both values on it with the horizontal at least the vertical, type steps by a quarter of φ (rounded to the half pixel), and dialogs are 377, 610 or 987px wide. Settings is a golden rectangle, 987 × 610. `ui/lib/scale.test.ts` enforces, in `npm test`, that padding, margin, gap, inset, offsets and border-radius are on the scale and that every `font-size` is a token; widths, heights and line-heights follow the scale by convention (the token audit at the end names the exceptions).
keyCharacteristics: Near-black neutrals in six tonal steps (the website's ground, surfaces and hairlines), a dark theme by default and a full light theme.
One accent, Phosphor Amber, which the user can change. It is never decoration.
Eleven cable colours, one per kind of connection, used only to say "this is an SSH/RDP/… thing".
The system face for the whole interface; JetBrains Mono only for code, commands, keys, fingerprints and passcodes.
The brand kit's horizontal logo on the start screen and in Settings › About; its own amber and white stay inside it.
Fibonacci spacing (1 2 3 5 8 13 21 34px) and five type sizes, both enforced by a test.
Rounded panels on a darker window. Flat at rest; shadows only on floating layers.
Icon-only tool buttons with tooltips. Boxicons SVGs. Session and folder icons move on hover; interface icons only spin or pulse while something waits.
Right-to-left ready: logical properties throughout, with flips for chevrons, menus and carets.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber says "you are here" or "you picked this", and nothing else. Two exceptions: the fill of a dialog's single primary button, and a folder's tag (`.tag`, `prod`, `lab`…), which is a fact about where you are and shows on the folder's row and under a pane. No amber headings, icons or decorative strokes. The start screen's prompt sigil and block cursor are the website's: they say where you type.

rules.name: The Logo Colours Rule
rules.body: The logo's own amber, `#FFC20E`, and its white (`--mark`) live only in the logo. The brand amber is not the accent and is never UI state, as the website's One Phosphor Rule says; the accent is the phosphor `--gold`. `ui/lib/Logo.svelte` swaps the artwork's `#F2F2F2` fills for `currentColor`, which is `--mark`, so one file serves both themes; the small amber tile is never recoloured.

rules.name: The Cable Colour Rule
rules.body: A kind hue identifies a kind of connection and nothing else, and nothing else takes its place: a session's icon is always in its kind's hue, whatever it is marked with. State (connected, waiting, failed) is always `ok` / `warn` / `error`, never a kind hue.

rules.name: The See-Through Chrome Rule
rules.body: Chrome backgrounds are written `rgba(var(--panel-rgb), var(--chrome-alpha))` (or the `window`/`bg`/`deep` triplet), never as a hex. `--chrome-alpha` drops below 1 while the Transparent effect is on, and the desktop shows through. Any place is two layers, the window's ground and a panel or terminal on it, and `--chrome-alpha` is worked out so the two together make the Opacity setting, in every window: don't paint a third layer between them. A floating layer is one layer at `--float-alpha`, over what's already there, as a window is over another. The lock screen stays solid: it hides what's behind it. `--solid` (1, or 0 with the Transparent effect) switches off the active tab's and a detached window's own fill so the pane shows through. The title bar is the one place with only the ground under it, so a dark desktop turns it grey on light: there its icons (`--bar-ink`) go from `weak` to ink while `--solid` is 0, and the palette field and the New session key are a second layer at `--chrome-alpha`, as a panel is, instead of solid slabs on it. On light the New session key is `deep` (white, as the field), since `raised` is barely off the bar's grey. Two exceptions, named: the scrim behind a dialog (`--scrim`) and the palette (`--scrim-soft`) is the dark ground at 0.4 and 0.32 (black at 0.18 and 0.12 on light), and the RDP view's bars over the picture use fixed dark greys (`#0c0c0c`, `rgb(12 12 12 / 0.75)`), because they sit on the remote desktop's black, not on chrome.

rules.name: The Five Sizes Rule
rules.body: Every `font-size` is a type token (`var(--t-s)` … `var(--t-xxl)`), `inherit`, an `em`, or a `clamp()`. A raw `px` size fails `npm test`.

rules.name: The Golden Line Rule
rules.body: Prose and text areas set `line-height: var(--phi)`. Dense UI text stays at 1.4.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Characters Rule
rules.body: The system face sets the interface; the mono is only for what is read character by character or must line up: code and commands (`code`, `pre`, `.mono`, snippets, previews), keys (`kbd`), a host key's fingerprint, the sign-in code, the Co-op passcode, addresses and traffic figures, and the start screen's prompt. A title, a button, a tag, a status line, a menu or a list is never in the mono, however short. A new surface takes the system face by inheriting from `body`; it does not set a `font-family` of its own, and there is no token for "short text".

rules.name: The Fibonacci Rule
rules.body: Padding, margin, gap, inset, offsets and border-radius values are Fibonacci pixels; a stray 4px or 12px there fails `npm test`. Widths, heights and line-heights are not tested: keep them on the scale or derived, or name the exception (pane sizers 6px, scrollbars 10px, the title bar's 46px Windows buttons, `progress` 4px).

rules.name: The Derived Value Rule
rules.body: A value worked out from others is written as `calc(…)` from the tokens it comes from, so it reads as derived and follows them: `calc(8px + var(--icon-s) + var(--gap))` is a search field's text start past its 16px icon (`--icon` is the 18px of controls and rows), `calc(var(--r-menu) - 3px)` a menu item's corner, and `calc(var(--control) + 2 * var(--gap) + 2px)` the collapsed rail.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface casts a shadow only if it floats over the work and goes away again, and takes it from one of the three tokens. Panels, tabs, rows and buttons never do.

rules.name: The Nested Curve Rule
rules.body: A rounded thing inside another keeps the same curve: its radius is the outer one less the room between them, written as `calc()` (a menu item is `calc(var(--r-menu) - 3px)`, the kind glyph in the session editor `calc(var(--r-control) - 2px)`), and never below `--r-control`: a row inside an 8px-radius, 8px-padded panel keeps 3px.

dos: **Do** use only Fibonacci pixels for spacing and radii (1 2 3 5 8 13 21 34), with padding pairs on the scale, horizontal at least vertical (`3px 8px`, `5px 8px`, `8px 13px`).
**Do** set every text size from the type tokens (`--t-s --t --t-l --t-xl --t-xxl`).
**Do** size things with `--row` (21px), `--control` (26px) and `--bar` (34px), and write any derived value as `calc(…)`.
**Do** keep amber for focus, selection, toggles that are on, links, drop targets and the one primary action. Read it as `var(--gold)`, since the user can change it.
**Do** colour a session by its kind hue (icon, tab connector, glyph tile) through `--kind`.
**Do** paint chrome as `rgba(var(--…-rgb), var(--chrome-alpha))` so the Transparent effect shows through.
**Do** end a menu with its destructive item (`.danger`) and start groups with `.sep`.
**Do** offer Undo instead of a question when the thing can be put back, and ask (with a danger button) only when it can't: a running connection, a folder of sessions, a restore.

**Do** focus the safe answer when yes can't be undone or is a security call (Cancel on a delete or restore, Keep editing on discard), so Enter never does the irreversible thing; an ordinary yes (Close tab, which Reopen can undo) keeps the focus. The one security call that focuses yes is trusting a host, RDP server or BMC seen for the first time (Trust, as ssh's "yes"); a key that changed is refused whatever is answered.
**Do** make tool buttons icon-only with a tooltip.

**Do** keep motion to state and continuity, in three durations: `--quick` (0.1s) for an exit, `--move` (0.16s) for an arrival or a change of state, `--glide` (0.2s) for a thing moving to another place; arrivals on `--ease-out`, a new floating layer through `float-in`, exits faster than entrances. The longer ones are named: the welcome leaving in 0.12s, the Co-op ring's 0.3s line and seat glide and its 0.5s packets, the 2.6s fade of a found setting. When one view replaces another (the start screen giving way to the shell typed into it), the old one leaves first and the new one arrives after it. CSS motion stops under `prefers-reduced-motion` through `ui/app.css`; a Svelte transition must check it itself.
**Do** use logical properties (`inset-inline-*`, `margin-inline-*`) so right-to-left mirrors.

**Do** leave the interface in the system face (`var(--ui)`, inherited from `body`) and use `var(--mono)` only for what is read character by character: code, commands, keys, fingerprints, passcodes and figures that must line up.
**Do** show the logo through `Logo.svelte`, so its tiles and wordmark follow the theme through `--mark`.
donts: **Don't** use off-scale spacing (4px, 6px, 10px, 12px, 16px) in padding, margin, gap, inset, offsets or radii, or a raw `font-size` in px; the scale test fails on those. Sizes (width, height, line-height) aren't tested: keep them on the scale or name the exception.
**Don't** put a shadow on a resting panel, tab, row or button or write a new shadow value for a floating layer: use `--shadow-float`, `--shadow-menu` or `--shadow-dialog`.
**Don't** use amber for headings, icons, illustration or large fills other than the primary button.
**Don't** use a kind hue to show state, or a status colour to mean a kind of connection.
**Don't** let a user's colour recolour a session's icon: marks go on names (`.tinted`) and tab lines, and accent presets stay off the kind hues and the error red.
**Don't** hard-code the accent's hex (but for the Amber (default) swatch in Settings › Appearance), or the chrome as an opaque hex.
**Don't** animate the interface's own icons, bar a spinner or a pulse that says something is waiting. Only session and folder icons move for their own sake, and only on hover.
**Don't** add big padding or wide gaps. The densest comfortable layout is the house style.
**Don't** set a title, button, tag, status line, menu or list in the mono, or bring back a token for "short text": the interface is one face.
**Don't** use the logo's amber `#FFC20E` or `--mark` outside the logo, or recolour, stretch, rotate or add effects to the logo.
